name: Quilboar
summary: Across central Kalimdor, Quilboar defend their lands with sharp quills and fierce resolve. They claim descent from Agamaggan and dwell in thorn mazes across Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens. Their struggles over water, soil, and sacred ground threaten travelers and Horde settlements.

sections.title: Children of the Great Boar
sections.body:
Quilboar honor Agamaggan, the colossal boar Ancient who died fighting the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Their sacred traditions call them his mortal offspring.

Where Agamaggan bled and died across central Kalimdor, enormous thorny vines burst from scorched earth and formed sprawling root mazes. Quilboar hold these places sacred. Across the Barrens, his crystallized blood remains as crimson Blood Shards. Quilboar geomancers dig them up and honor them as powerful talismans.

sections.title: Bramble Harrows and Geomancy
sections.body:
Quilboar build no towns of stone or timber. Instead, they grow colossal briars that choke nearby plants and leave the ground barren. Each tribe is usually guided by powerful geomancers. These practitioners follow a crude, earthbound shamanism, consulting stones and crystals to guide their clan. They call on Agamaggan's spirit to send spectral boars into battle.

The arid central plains have few oases, so quilboar prize water above all. When rare rains come, they hold lavish feasts. They defend their water holes fiercely.

sections.title: The War for the Barrens
sections.body:
For generations, quilboar have clashed with nomadic tauren and roaming centaur packs. When Thrall led the Orcish Horde into Kalimdor, orcs quickly settled Durotar and opened trade routes through the Barrens. Displaced quilboar tribes rose in revolt.

Their war parties ambush supply wagons, are suspected of driving tallstriders into wagon trains, and raid outposts such as Crossroads and Camp Taurajo. Two tribes dominate the open plains: the Razormane and the Bristleback. Both fight the Horde and each other.

sections.title: The Shadow over Razorfen
sections.body:
Razorfen Kraul and nearby Razorfen Downs lie on the Barrens' southern edge, at the spiritual heart of quilboar civilization. Agamaggan's gargantuan remains formed these tangled mazes. An ambitious crone named Charlga Razorflank seized the Kraul and directed attacks on rival clans and Horde territories.

Razorfen Downs, the traditional quilboar capital, has fallen to the Scourge. The corrupted Death's Head quilboar joined the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer and succumbed to undeath. Now the ancestral tomb is a plague-ridden stronghold.

faq.q: Why do quilboar hate the Horde so much?
faq.answer: The Horde displaced quilboar when Thrall's people landed and claimed land for Orgrimmar. Quilboar had occupied Durotar and the Barrens' fertile oases and thorned ravines long before the Horde arrived. Now the tribes see every caravan, outpost, and water well as stolen ancestral ground.

faq.q: What is the relationship between quilboar and Agamaggan?
faq.answer: Agamaggan is a colossal boar Ancient who fought the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Quilboar claim descent from him. The great briars they inhabit sprang up where his blood soaked the earth, and the sacred tunnels of Razorfen Downs are said to be carved from his remains.

faq.q: What are the red stones quilboar carry?
faq.answer: The red crystals are Blood Shards, formed from Agamaggan's petrified blood. Quilboar dig them up across the Barrens, believing they hold the vitality and strength of their fallen ancestor. Geomancers use them to fuel earth rituals and battle enchantments.

faq.q: What kind of magic do quilboar use?
faq.answer: Quilboar practice geomancy, an elemental craft like crude shamanism, centered on stone, earth, and thorns. They prize the reading of stones and gems above other mystical arts. Tribal geomancers call on earth spirits, summon brambles to snare foes, and conjure boar spirits in Agamaggan's image.

faq.q: Why are quilboar so protective of water?
faq.answer: The Barrens is arid, with very few natural springs and oases. Quilboar regard water as survival, wealth, and spiritual blessing. They feast even when light desert rains fall and fiercely guard springs from approaching caravans and herds.

faq.q: What is the difference between Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs?
faq.answer: Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs are vast briar mazes in southern Kalimdor, grown from Agamaggan's carcass. Razorfen Kraul is the stronghold of the crone Charlga Razorflank, who rallies living quilboar against outsiders. Razorfen Downs was the quilboar ancestral capital. Now the Scourge lich Amnennar the Coldbringer rules there and raises dead quilboar as undead minions.

angles.text: As a tauren, your ancestors fought quilboar for watering holes and grazing land long before the orcs sailed west. Their spreading briars choke the natural earth sustained by the Earth Mother.
As an orc, securing Durotar and the Barrens means breaking quilboar war bands. Their raids keep harassing Horde trade wagons and outlying farmsteads.
As a shaman, you can see quilboar geomancy as an earthy, ancient branch of shamanic tradition, turned toward territorial brutality and the summoning of savage boar spirits.
As a member of the Horde, you face quilboar ambushes along vital caravans between Orgrimmar, the Crossroads, and Thunder Bluff. Their presence threatens supply routes across central Kalimdor.
